chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abdullah ibn Muskan from Abu Basir who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "The boundary of Arafat is from the two Ma'zamin to the furthest point of the standing (waqf)."

key_terms.الْمَأْزَمَيْنِ: The two Ma'zamin, a specific landmark used as a boundary marker
key_terms.الْمَوْقِفِ: The standing (waqf), the ritual act of standing at Arafat
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the plain where the main pillar of Hajj (Waqf) takes place

ai.seo_question: What are the defined boundaries of Arafat for Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* precisely delineates the spatial limits of the *Waqf* at Arafat, a critical determinant for the validity of Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence. By anchoring the boundary between the two *Ma'zamin* and the furthest point of the standing area, it provides the practical legal framework for pilgrims to ensure their ritual presence fulfills the divine command.
